hook_text: If the Earth were an apple, everything we have ever built would sit on a layer thinner than its skin.
clip_script: Magaliesberg, North West. Bare grey rock up top: very hard and very old. Below the trail: soft brown soil. Dig a little hole: roots, a beetle, an earthworm. All of this sits on the crust, the Earth's thin rocky skin, with the hot mantle and the metal core deep below. Rock is hard. Soil is loose. And four things keep the whole hillside alive: soil, air, water and sunlight.
visual_style: Whiteboard cut-away Earth with crust, mantle and core, then a close-up of soil with roots and an earthworm.
mood: Outdoorsy and curious, like a hike with a great guide.
pacing: Zoom out to the whole Earth, then zoom in to a handful of soil.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and dig a little hole to see what lives in your soil.
